page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the ARMv8 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM Neoverse-V2 processor running at 3.0 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The hardware includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 4020 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across 10 local SSD drives. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark scored 86659.83, which is categorized in the top 25% tier, while the single-core performance of 1821.19 sits in the middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 5935.14 GB/sec and large block uncached read speeds at 334.84 GB/sec. Large block write speeds reached 158.43 GB/sec. Data decompression is also highly efficient, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression measured at 532.16 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highmem-48-lssd offers high resource density by combining a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with substantial local NVMe storage. However, architectural tradeoffs must be considered. The ARM64 Neoverse-V2 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX, which may limit compatibility with certain legacy software or specialized vector workloads. Additionally, the lack of hyperthreading means each of the 48 vCPUs maps directly to a single physical core, ensuring dedicated execution resources but lacking the thread-level concurrency of simultaneous multithreading.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. The combination of 384 GB of RAM and 4020 GB of low-latency local NVMe SSD storage makes it suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
